title: Negative at this exposure: growing sink discs (1 per 200 t, R 24) let mar-40 Marangoni rods escape more often than mar-0 rods (6/7 and 3/5 vs 1/3) but catch only 3-7 bodies per run, and the selection gradient on per-cycle swim distance at fixed speed is not positive (-0.14, -0.15 in S vs -0.03 in the removal control)
summary: Forked c34's Marangoni rods so the chemostat target is a field lowered to -1.2 inside growing sink discs (Poisson, one per 200 t, 0.08 px/t to R 24, RNG seeded only by seed); arm S lets caught bodies dissolve or escape, arm I removes them when the disc opens. phi_in -1.2 dissolves caught bodies before the disc closes (tuning, mar 0). T=1600: escape share 0.86 (6/7, seed 90) and 0.60 (3/5, seed 91) at mar 40 against 0.33 (1/3) at mar 0 (seed 90); persistent splits 29-38 in every run. The regression of relative descendants (two median cycles after birth) on standardized D, speed and straightness gives a D gradient of -0.14 [-0.49,+0.05] and -0.15 [-0.34,+0.05] in S and -0.03 in I on both seeds, so the environment does not reward distance per cycle at this exposure: a disc catches about one body, and the long-cycle cost of swimming far dominates.

finding.operator: growing sink discs in the chemostat target (escape environment) for the Marangoni rods
finding.control: arm I (same disc stream, caught bodies removed at opening), and arm S at mar 0
finding.result: escape share 0.86 and 0.60 (mar 40) vs 0.33 (mar 0, n=3); bodies caught 3-7 per run; D gradient at fixed speed -0.14, -0.15 (S) vs -0.03, -0.03 (I)
